price_per_million.source: copied from reasoning_models_v1 (confirmed 2026-11-11); thinking tokens billed as output

research_concepts: offensive reorganization (shift in association structure / play-type fingerprint vs baseline)
structural influence load L (leave-one-out predicted reorganization)
change in points per possession (PPP) during absence
methodological_questions: Does the magnitude of observed reorganization, or its size relative to L, predict the change in PPP across absence spells?
Is the reorganization measure reliable and is it mechanically tied to PPP, since both are computed from the same possessions?
Is the association confounded by absent-player quality, opponent, rest or regression to the mean?
Is n=148 spells enough, given franchise clustering and noisy per-spell PPP?

historical_evidence.finding: Absence validation. V1 (real absences move the association structure) was confirmed: 16/23 above the own-null p95, binomial p=2.67e-16, mean excess +0.142 CI [+0.103,+0.187]. V2 (L predicts the magnitude of real reorganization) failed: rho=+0.288, p=0.077, CI [-0.244,+0.667]; partial rho=+0.253, p=0.115. It was flagged UNDERPOWERED with n=23 player-seasons and 18 franchises (below the ~20 floor). Dropping 2 absorption cases gave rho=+0.444. The L_pred vs recomputed LOO rho was +0.93 (measurement faithful). A record note says a later full-pool run reversed V2. The family is auto-adjudicated and members disagree (supported, failed_gate, inconclusive, null).
Play-type replacement similarity did not separate absorption from cascade (Spearman -0.19, wrong-signed). Verdict recorded as null (B_powered_null), with a label-error risk.

Defensive analogue: among 653 eligible, corr(D_A, dPPP_allowed)=+0.020. Opponent-fingerprint displacement did not track PPP allowed. The record notes a mechanical-floor risk (corr(D_A, n_on)=-0.475 before eligibility filtering).
Shaper absence displaces the team fingerprint (D_A) more than a usage-matched role occupant (+0.115, 96 pairs). r(L, D_A)=+0.60. The outcome is displacement, not PPP.
Connector absence displaces offensive identity more than usage-matched others (n=96). The outcome is displacement, not PPP. The record lists small-sample and mechanical-floor risks.
Team association structure persists across split halves beyond play-type rates (S=0.352). Structure is a stable, measurable property.
Structural influence is not reducible to usage (residual share ~0.90), and residual influence is split-half stable (rho ~+0.67). The record lists a measurement-reliability risk.
Model-scored (not observed) player routing: A5 vs A3 gain shrank from +0.94 to +0.03 pts/100 on the larger sample. Powered null.
Holdout play-type rank validation (median rho +0.539). The record's failure mechanism is C_artifact, since the top-3 lift partly reflects league-wide high-efficiency play types, and it flags drift.
Single-game relative-structure validation with 4-35 possessions per play type was unanswerable at that sample.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Testing whether L predicts the magnitude of observed reorganization (V2) with 23 player-seasons from 18 franchises
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as A_unanswerable: below the registered ~20-franchise floor, CI width ~0.9, over-predicts for replaceable centers (absorption cases).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using teammate play-type similarity to separate absorption from cascade
failed_approaches.why: Powered null; a similar teammate is almost always findable; label/classification error.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Linking fingerprint displacement (D_A) to PPP allowed on the defensive side
failed_approaches.why: Powered null (corr +0.020, n=653), with a mechanical coupling to exposure (n_on) that required eligibility filtering.
Powered null; the effect was model-scored, not observed, and shrank with sample size.

evidence_establishes: Real absences reorganize the association structure well beyond a noise floor (FAM:SF20 V1, confirmed with a very small p).
Reorganization magnitude is measurable and the structure is persistent and stable (FAM:SF17, FAM:SF18).
The L-predicted magnitude has not been shown to track observed reorganization at n=23 (FAM:SF20 V2, underpowered, inconclusive).
The one retrieved test linking a fingerprint displacement to a PPP outcome (defensive side, FAM:SF-PAP-030) was a powered null.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether the size of offensive reorganization, raw or relative to L, predicts the change in offensive PPP; no retrieved record tests this directly.
The direction of any such relationship (bigger reorganization could mean cascade and worse PPP, or successful adaptation).
Whether the later full-pool V2 reversal noted in FAM:SF20 holds; its numbers are not given in the record.
Whether the 148-spell sample overlaps the 23 player-seasons used before.
own_inferences: No retrieved record answers this question, so the prior work is a related-but-different result and not an answer.

'Relative to L' is ambiguous. It could mean the residual (observed D minus L-predicted D), a ratio, or D as the outcome of L. I read it as observed reorganization compared with the L-predicted amount, and the design registers one primary reading.
Because the play-type mix drives PPP mechanically (high-efficiency types like CUT, PUTBACK and TRANSITION), any raw D-to-dPPP correlation risks being partly mechanical.
Absent-player quality drives both D and dPPP, so confounding is likely to inflate any correlation unless absent-player value is controlled.

With n=148 the minimum detectable rho is about 0.23 for independent spells (two-sided alpha=0.05, 80% power). The true PPP effect of reorganization is probably small, since the defensive analogue was ~0, and spell PPP is noisy, so a null would be hard to separate from low power.
The question is testable only in a weak sense: a positive result needs a rho of at least 0.25 after controls, and a null can only exclude large effects.
uncertainties: The exact definition of reorganization and L, and the direction of the hypothesis, are not given in the task.
What the 986 units represent is not stated (perhaps candidate player-seasons, with 148 passing the spell filters).
Possessions per spell and the franchise count within the 148 spells are unknown, so the effective sample after clustering is unknown.
The overlap with the 23 spells already used in FAM:SF20 is unknown.
The record statuses are auto-adjudicated (confidence 0.55 for FAM:SF20), and members disagree.

historical_effect.explanation: Without the history I might have proceeded as a direct correlational test. The history shows that (a) the closest earlier magnitude test was killed by underpower (18 franchises, CI width 0.9), (b) a fingerprint-to-PPP link on the defensive side was a powered null with a mechanical-floor problem, and (c) play-type-based outcomes carry composition artifacts. So I choose proceed_with_changes: franchise-aware power, a mix-adjusted PPP outcome, controls for absent-player value, a pre-specified reading of 'relative to L', and a null reported as a bound, not as absence of effect.

methodological_questions: Does the magnitude of offensive reorganization relative to baseline L predict the change in points per possession?
How is reorganization measured and is the measure reliable given small possession counts per spell?
Is the reorganization-to-efficiency association confounded by absent player quality, opponent, or regression to the mean?
Is the outcome mechanically linked to the reorganization measure (play-type points derived from the same possessions)?
Is sample size of 148 spells sufficient to detect a correlation?
args.query: player absence offensive reorganization magnitude relative to baseline predicts change in points per possession across absence spells

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
How much the offense reorganizes (relative to L) predicts the change in points per possession.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=986; n=148, mde rho; 148 spells

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

Stage 1. Reply only with the retrieval call: {"action": "tool", "tool": "retrieve_history", "args": {"research_concepts": ["..."], "methodological_questions": ["..."], "query": "..."}}

reasoning_details.text:
I'm settling on the final framing: whether the offense's reorganization, measured relative to its structural influence load, predicts the change in PPP. The earlier test of reorganization against that load was underpowered, and nothing I've retrieved tests reorganization against the PPP change directly. The closest analog is the defensive study, where the corresponding correlation came out null and carried a risk from mechanical floors.

I'm weighing the odds that this gets supported, rejected, or comes out as an artifact, and I'm leaning toward proceeding with changes. The design needs a stated estimand: "relative to L" is ambiguous, so I'll pre-register both the raw reorganization measure and its residual after the load prediction, and distinguish the PPP change from the same team's matched baseline.

I'm now working through the risks of testing this. The main worry is a mechanical link: the reorganization is measured from the same possessions that produce PPP, so a shift toward lower-efficiency play types would move PPP by itself. I'm weighing how to separate the two, either with an odd/even possession split or by residualizing the PPP change on the league's expected PPP for the play-type mix. I also need to control for the absent player's own offensive value, since a high-impact absence could drive both the reorganization and the PPP drop.

I'm setting the estimand as signed ΔPPP with a two-sided test, since I haven't committed to a predicted direction, and I'm freezing the data through the 2026-11-01 cutoff and treating playoffs separately. The 23 prior spells overlap with this sample, so I'll reuse them but note that they aren't independent, and I'm weighing whether the effective sample is smaller once clustering is accounted for.
